Article 20

Provision of services and advanced referral handling as referred to in Article 17 letter b is intended for:
a. women victims of domestic violence; b. women victims of criminal acts of trafficking in persons; c. women in emergency situations and special conditions; andd. women victims of other acts of violence requiring coordination at the Regency level.

Article 14

1. Women's empowerment in the economic field is implemented by means including:a. facilitating women in efforts to improve family economy;
b. may provide capital assistance to women, especially migrant workers, women in remote areas, women as heads of households, and women victims of domestic violence; andc. implementing home industry and non-agricultural industry development programs.
2. Procedures for providing capital assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 18

( 1 ) Prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 17 letter a is implemented by means of increasing family and community awareness.

( 2 ) Increasing family and community awareness as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out in an integrated and continuous manner in the form of socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling.

( 3 ) Socialization, guidance and training, and/or counseling as referred to in paragraph (2) is implemented by technical Regional Apparatus responsible for the field, institutions, organizations, mass media, business sector, academics, law enforcement, community and Regional Technical Implementation Units in accordance with their duties and functions.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality hereinafter abbreviated as KG is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Gender Analysis is a process built systematically to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access to and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy. 8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension -3- of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region. 9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget hereinafter abbreviated as ARG is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, tribes, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce the immune system of humans until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victims of Kidnapping are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state. 5-

29. Child Victims of Sale are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to another party for compensation or other reasons. 30.

Article 17

Protection of Women is carried out by means of: a. prevention of violence against women;
b. provision of services and advanced referral handling; andc. strengthening and development of institutions providing women's protection services.
13-

Article 19

1. In addition to prevention of violence against women as referred to in Article 18, efforts to prevent violence against women are carried out by increasing women's insight, knowledge, skills, and independence.
2. Prevention of violence against women as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by means of:a. increasing informal education;
b. opening accessibility to obtain education, training, funding, income enhancement, and social services; andc. providing access to informal employment for women.

Article 78

1. Monitoring as referred to in Article 76 -37- paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out by:a. observing and identifying the development of cases of physical and/or psychological violence against Children;
b. anticipating problems arising from cases of physical and/or psychological violence against Children;andc. following up on cases of physical and/or psychological violence against Children.
2. Reporting as referred to in Article 76 paragraph (1) letter b shall be carried out periodically or at any time according to needs.
3. Imposition of sanctions as referred to in Article 76 paragraph (1) letter b shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Child Victims of Trafficking are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited. 31. Child Victims of Physical Violence are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury. 32. Child Victims of Psychological Violence are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering. 33. Child Victims of Sexual Crimes are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 34. Child Victims of Terrorism Networks are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by acts of terrorism either as Child victims, Child perpetrators, Children of perpetrators, and Child witnesses. 35. Children with Disabilities are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 36. Child Victims of Maltreatment are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially. 37. Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process. 38. Children with Deviant Social Behavior are Children who have attitudes and behaviors that do not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, show irresponsible attitudes and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violate the rights and norms that live in society. 39. Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a bad stamp or view from labeling related to the condition of their parents. 40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for Children. 41. Educational Institution is an educational unit as referred to in laws and regulations concerning the national education system. 42. Counseling is a process carried out in the form of interviews to help Children understand themselves better, so that Children can overcome difficulties in adjusting themselves to various roles and relationships and find appropriate problem solving. 43. Social Assistance is a dynamic interaction between social workers and Children who need Special Protection to jointly face and solve social problems faced. 44. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable Children to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life. 45. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing Children who need Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment. 46. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is a child protection strategy by integrating children's rights into every development activity from the preparation of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of various laws and regulations, policies, programs, and activities by applying the principle of the best interests of the child. 47. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion, which directly or indirectly -7- is based on differentiation in humans on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, legal status of children, and physical and/or mental conditions that result in reduction, deviation, or elimination, recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, socio-cultural fields and other aspects of life. 48. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of someone by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 50. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 52. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.

Article 43

1. Special Protection for Children from Minority and Isolated Groups so that they do not experience violence, discrimination, and other mistreatment as referred to in Article 41 shall be carried out through preventive measures.
2. Preventive measures as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through:a. provision of education to the community;and b. coordination with the Regency Government.  c. preventive measures as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
3. Preventive measures as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 118

To prevent the occurrence of stigmatization from labeling of Children related to the condition of their parents, the Regency Government shall:
a. provide education to the Community and play an active role in eliminating stigma against Children who are labeled related to the condition of their parents;

b.provide space for Children who are labeled related to the condition of -48- their parents to obtain recreational activities; and
c. coordinate with service units that handle the protection of Children who are labeled related to the condition of their parents in the event of potential violence and discrimination against Children in the Regency.

Article 102

Special Protection for Child Victims of Maltreatment and Child Victims of Neglect as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (1) letter m shall be carried out through efforts of supervision, prevention, care, Counseling, Social Rehabilitation, and Social Assistance.

Paragraph 9

Child Victims of Physical and/or Psychological Violence

Article 37

1. Provision of legal assistance and other assistance effectively as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter c shall be provided in the form of:a. legal consultation, legal accompaniment, and defense in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations;
b. provision of language interpreters for Children in legal proceedings including sign language interpreters for Children with Disabilities;
c. provision of information regarding the development of their case in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations; andd. provision of legal assistance and other assistance effectively in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
2. Implementation of recreational activities as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter d shall consist of daily free physical exercise activities in open spaces, daily entertainment activities, arts, or developing skills.
3. Avoidance of arrest, detention, or imprisonment as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter g shall be carried out with attention to the age of the child, type of crime committed, threat of crime committed, and their criminal responsibility.
4. Provision of justice before a Children's court that is objective, impartial, and in a closed hearing -24- to the public as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter h shall be carried out by seeking a child-friendly court with standard facilities and infrastructure in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
5. Avoidance of publication of their identity as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter i shall be carried out by keeping confidential the name of the Child in Conflict with the Law, parents' names, address, face, and other matters that may reveal the identity of the Child in Conflict with the Law.
6. Provision of accompaniment by parents/guardians and persons trusted by the Child as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter j shall be carried out to assist and provide support to the Child so that they are ready to follow the investigation, prosecution, and examination process in court proceedings.
7. Provision of social advocacy as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter k is intended to protect and defend Children in Conflict with the Law provided in the form of awareness of rights and obligations, defense, and fulfillment of rights.
8. Provision of health services as referred to in Article 36 paragraph (1) letter o shall be carried out in promotive, preventive, curative, and rehabilitative forms in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations in the health sector.

Article 120

( 1 ) The provision of referral services or further handling as referred to in Article 119 letter a shall be intended for child victims of violence who require coordination at the Regency level.

( 2 ) The provision of referral services or handling as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out through the PPA unit at the Regency level.

( 3 ) Further provisions regarding the duties, membership, and establishment of the PPA unit as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 21

( 1 ) In addition to the provision of services and referral service handling as referred to in Article 20, the Regency Government is obliged to provide special services for:
a. women who are included in vulnerable and/or minority groups;
b. elderly women; andc. women with special needs.
2. Special services as referred to in paragraph (1) are provided in the form of:a. ease in obtaining and enjoying their rights in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations;
b. ease in access to economic resources and natural resources, social security, and basic public services; andc. provision of specific needs of women in emergency situations and special conditions.
3. Further provisions regarding special services as referred to in paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 51. CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality hereinafter abbreviated as KG is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Gender Analysis is a process built systematically to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access to and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy. 8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension -3- of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region. 9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget hereinafter abbreviated as ARG is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, tribes, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce the immune system of humans until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victims of Kidnapping are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state. 5-

29. Child Victims of Sale are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to another party for compensation or other reasons. 30.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality hereinafter abbreviated as KG is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Gender Analysis is a process built systematically to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access to and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy. 8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension -3- of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region. 9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget hereinafter abbreviated as ARG is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, tribes, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce the immune system of humans until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victims of Kidnapping are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state. 5-

Child Victims of Trafficking are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited. 31. Child Victims of Physical Violence are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury. 32. Child Victims of Psychological Violence are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering. 33. Child Victims of Sexual Crimes are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 34. Child Victims of Terrorism Networks are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by acts of terrorism either as Child victims, Child perpetrators, Children of perpetrators, and Child witnesses. 35. Children with Disabilities are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 36. Child Victims of Maltreatment are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially. 37. Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process. 38. Children with Deviant Social Behavior are Children who have attitudes and behaviors that do not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, show irresponsible attitudes and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violate the rights and norms that live in society. 39. Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a bad stamp or view from labeling related to the condition of their parents. 40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for Children. 41. Educational Institution is an educational unit as referred to in laws and regulations concerning the national education system. 42. Counseling is a process carried out in the form of interviews to help Children understand themselves better, so that Children can overcome difficulties in adjusting themselves to various roles and relationships and find appropriate problem solving. 43. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable Children to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life. 45. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing Children who need Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment. 46. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is a child protection strategy by integrating children's rights into every development activity from the preparation of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of various laws and regulations, policies, programs, and activities by applying the principle of the best interests of the child. 47. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion, which directly or indirectly -7- is based on differentiation in humans on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, legal status of children, and physical and/or mental conditions that result in reduction, deviation, or elimination, recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, socio-cultural fields and other aspects of life. 48. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of someone by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 50. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 52. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality hereinafter abbreviated as KG is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Child Victims of Trafficking are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited. 31. Child Victims of Physical Violence are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury. 32. Child Victims of Sexual Crimes are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 34. Children with Disabilities are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 36. Child Victims of Maltreatment are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially. 37. Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process. 38. Children with Deviant Social Behavior are Children who have attitudes and behaviors that do not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, show irresponsible attitudes and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violate the rights and norms that live in society. 39. Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a bad stamp or view from labeling related to the condition of their parents. 40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for Children. 41. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality hereinafter abbreviated as KG is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Child Victims of Trafficking are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited. 31. Child Victims of Physical Violence are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury. 32. Child Victims of Psychological Violence are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering. 33. Child Victims of Sexual Crimes are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 34. Child Victims of Terrorism Networks are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by acts of terrorism either as Child victims, Child perpetrators, Children of perpetrators, and Child witnesses. 35. Children with Disabilities are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 36. Child Victims of Maltreatment are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially. 37. Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process. 38. Children with Deviant Social Behavior are Children who have attitudes and behaviors that do not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, show irresponsible attitudes and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violate the rights and norms that live in society. 39. Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a bad stamp or view from labeling related to the condition of their parents. 40. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 50. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 51. Article 1

Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality hereinafter abbreviated as KG is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget hereinafter abbreviated as ARG is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, tribes, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce the immune system of humans until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victims of Kidnapping are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state. 5-

Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of someone by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 49. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 52. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce the immune system of humans until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victims of Kidnapping are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state. 5-

Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of someone by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 50. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 51. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Regency. 5. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society. 6. Gender Equality hereinafter abbreviated as KG is the equality of conditions for men and women to obtain opportunities and their rights as human beings, so that they are able to play a role and participate in political, economic, socio-cultural, defense and security activities and equality in enjoying the results of development. 7. Gender Analysis is a process built systematically to identify and understand the division of labor or roles of men and women, access to and control over development resources, participation in the development process and the benefits they enjoy. 8. Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter abbreviated as PUG is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension -3- of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of policies, programs and development activities in the region. 9. Gender responsive is a policy, program, activity, and budgeting that reduces differences, needs, experiences, and aspirations of men and women. 10. Gender Responsive Budget hereinafter abbreviated as ARG is a budget that is responsive to the needs of women and men with the aim of realizing gender equality and justice. 11. Women's empowerment is an effort by women to obtain access and control over resources, economic, political, social, cultural, so that women can organize themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and participate actively in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 12. Protection of women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child who is still in the womb. 14. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 15. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 16. Violence is any unlawful act that results in suffering or pain physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens and/or endangers life and body and degrades dignity. 17. Special Protection for Children is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development. 18. Children in Emergency Situations are Children who are in environmental situations that threaten and disrupt the life and livelihood of Children caused by natural, non-natural, and/or social factors. 19. Children in Conflict with the Law are Children who are in conflict with the law, Children who are victims of criminal acts, and Children who are witnesses to criminal acts. 20. Children from Minority and Isolated Groups are Children who are left behind, at the forefront, outermost in an environment with different cultures, traditions, tribes, races, religions from other children whose numbers are far fewer than Children of other groups. 21. Children Who Are Economically Exploited are Children who are victims of acts of prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of Children by other parties or other similar actions to obtain material benefits. 22. Children Who Are Sexually Exploited are Children who are exploited to obtain benefits through sexual organs or other body organs of Children, including but not limited to all prostitution and indecency activities. 23. Children Who Are Victims of Narcotics, Alcohol, Psychotropic, and Other Addictive Substances Abuse are Children who are persuaded, deceived, tricked, forced, and/or threatened to use narcotics, alcohol, psychotropics, and other addictive substances. 24. Children Who Are Victims of Pornography are Children who experience trauma or suffering as a result of pornography crimes. 25. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce the immune system of humans until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome occurs. 26. Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome hereinafter abbreviated as AIDS is a collection of symptoms of reduced self-defense ability caused by the entry of the HIV virus into a person's body. 27. Children with HIV and AIDS are Children who are infected with HIV and/or AIDS either transmitted from parents or from other risk factors. 28. Child Victims of Kidnapping are Children who are taken by someone unlawfully with the intention of placing the Child under their power or the power of others or to place the Child in a helpless state. 5-

29. Child Victims of Sale are Children who are transferred by a person or group of people to another party for compensation or other reasons. 30.

Child Victims of Trafficking are Children who experience psychological, mental, physical, sexual, economic, and/or social suffering resulting from acts of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt with threats of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over the other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the Child being exploited. 31. Child Victims of Physical Violence are Children who experience violence that causes pain, illness, or serious injury. 32. Child Victims of Psychological Violence are Children who experience fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering. 33. Child Victims of Sexual Crimes are Children who experience forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural and/or unwanted manner, and forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes. 34. Child Victims of Terrorism Networks are Children who experience physical, mental suffering, and/or economic loss caused by acts of terrorism either as Child victims, Child perpetrators, Children of perpetrators, and Child witnesses. 35. Children with Disabilities are Children who experience physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 36. Child Victims of Maltreatment are Children who are threatened physically and non-physically due to acts of violence, mistreated or improperly treated in the family environment or their closest social environment, so that their basic needs are not properly fulfilled either physically, spiritually, or socially. 37. Child Victims of Neglect are Children who do not receive fulfillment of needs such as but not limited to health, safety, and welfare needs from parents or other persons who have legal responsibility to care for the Child resulting in harm in the Child's growth and development process. 38. Children with Deviant Social Behavior are Children who have attitudes and behaviors that do not consider the judgment and existence of other people in general around them, show irresponsible attitudes and lack of remorse regarding their mistakes, and often violate the rights and norms that live in society. 39. Children Who Are Victims of Stigmatization from Labeling related to the Condition of Their Parents are Children who are given negative social labels based on prejudice and aimed at separating, differentiating, discrediting, and ostracizing Children with a bad stamp or view from labeling related to the condition of their parents. 40. Substitute Family is foster parents, adoptive parents, and guardians who carry out the role and responsibility to provide alternative care for Children. 41. Educational Institution is an educational unit as referred to in laws and regulations concerning the national education system. 42. Counseling is a process carried out in the form of interviews to help Children understand themselves better, so that Children can overcome difficulties in adjusting themselves to various roles and relationships and find appropriate problem solving. 43. Social Assistance is a dynamic interaction between social workers and Children who need Special Protection to jointly face and solve social problems faced. 44. Social Rehabilitation is a process of refunctionalization and development to enable Children to be able to carry out their social functions properly in community life. 45. Social Reintegration is a process of preparing Children who need Special Protection to be able to return to the family and community environment. 46. Fulfillment of Children's Rights hereinafter abbreviated as PHA is a child protection strategy by integrating children's rights into every development activity from the preparation of planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of various laws and regulations, policies, programs, and activities by applying the principle of the best interests of the child. 47. Discrimination is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion, which directly or indirectly -7- is based on differentiation in humans on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, legal status of children, and physical and/or mental conditions that result in reduction, deviation, or elimination, recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, socio-cultural fields and other aspects of life. 48. Exploitation is an act with or without the consent of the victim which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, exploitation of physical sexual, reproductive organs or unlawfully transferring or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or exploiting the labor or abilities of someone by other parties to obtain material or immaterial benefits. 49. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 50. Guardian is a person or body who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 51. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 52. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations, business world.
